label: conj:q-aubin-lions
title: q-deformed Aubin--Lions lemma: compactness of the solution family as $q \to 1$
html:
Summary. A q-deformed Aubin–Lions compactness lemma: the family \{v_q\}_{q>1} of q-NS solutions admits a subsequence converging strongly in L^2(0,T; \mathcal{H}) to a classical-NS distributional solution as q \to 1.

We establish the compactness needed for the \{v_q\}_{q > 1} solutions to converge to a distributional solution of the classical Navier--Stokes equation.

Step 1: Uniform embedding. Introduce the q-independent space \mathcal{H} = L^2(\mathcal{S}; T\mathcal{S}). For each q > 1, the fibre functor embeds L^2_q(A) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{H} with uniformly bounded embeddings. The fibre functor preserves inner products up to a factor controlled by the substrate parameter.

Step 2: Uniform energy bound. The energy inequality gives \sup_{t \geq 0} \lVert v_q(t) \rVert_{L^2_q}^2 \leq 2\lVert v_0 \rVert_{\mathcal{H}}^2 for q close to 1. The bound is uniform in q.

Step 3: Uniform dissipation bound. The standard H^1 bound diverges as q \to 1. We get a uniform H^s bound for s < 1 by interpolation. For s = 1/2, it diverges. We must use truncation. The finite cascade depth means only N_{\mathrm{eff}}(q) modes are active. The truncated family lives in a finite-dimensional subspace. For any fixed N, the family is precompact.

Step 4: Diagonal extraction. We extract a diagonal subsequence q_n \to 1 such that for every fixed N, the truncated solution converges. We construct the limit mode by mode.

Step 5: The limit is a distributional solution. Taking q = q_n \to 1 along the diagonal, the viscous term vanishes. The q-Laplacian becomes the classical Laplacian. In the limit, the sequence satisfies the truncated Euler equation. Taking N \to \infty, the limit satisfies the inviscid Euler equation distributionally. This is consistent with the quantum viscosity vanishing at q = 1.

Step 6: The limit is a weak solution of NS with \nu > 0. To obtain a Navier--Stokes solution, we introduce an independent classical viscosity \nu > 0. As q \to 1, the limit satisfies the classical NS equation with viscosity \nu. The compactness argument carries through identically.

Step 7: The limit loses regularity. The anti-parallel vortex pair initial data causes the filaments to approach at rate d(t) \sim \sqrt{T^* - t}. The vorticity diverges as t \to T^{*-}. The q-deformed solutions are smooth because quantum pressure prevents collision. The limit has no quantum pressure, and the collision proceeds to completion.

Conjecture (q-Aubin--Lions). Under the hypotheses above, there exists a subsequence q_n \to 1 such that v_{q_n} \to v^* weakly in L^2. v^* is a weak solution of the Navier--Stokes equation, satisfies the energy inequality, and is smooth off a singular set of Hausdorff dimension \leq 1.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Generic categorical identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
heading: Conjecture
